audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagrees with the whys sitting next to it in five of seven rows. whys[0] says Crushing Blow out-trades you at 1 but the chart says Skill; whys[1] says level 2 is even but the chart says Jax; whys[3] says you stay ahead at 4-5 but the chart says Skill; whys[5] says Warrior Trickster scales in his favour at first item but the chart says Jax; whys[6] calls two items a pure coinflip but the chart says Jax.
audit.why: The packet chart (Wukong, Skill, Jax, Jax, Skill, Wukong, Skill) matches the prose exactly, and the 49.64% win rate over 1515 games supports a lane that ends even rather than one Jax owns from level 2 onward.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Wukong, Skill, Jax, Jax, Skill, Wukong, Skill across both layers as one atomic group, with ratings and the two now-contradictory phase whys rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is written "Grandmaster at Arms" in spikes[2].text, mid and late — his title, not the ability. wants.you[1] gets it half-right as "Grandmaster's".
audit.why: The ability is Grandmaster's Might, 110/100/90s; phases[4].why already uses the real name.
audit.corrected: Renamed in the three prose strings. Spike structure verified against the text: Wukong at 1 (Crushing Blow) and first item (Warrior Trickster), Jax at 3 and 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why still reads as a generic Trinity Force line on a row that now belongs to Wukong, and whys[3] claims Counter Strike is 'up more often' without the number that makes it true.
audit.why: Counter Strike drops from 17s at rank 1 to 13s at rank 3, which is exactly why maxing it through 4-5 covers more Nimbus Strike engages. The first-item row is Warrior Trickster's, not Trinity's: the decoy is what eats a mistimed Counter Strike, and that is the decisive interaction of the whole matchup.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why rewritten around Warrior Trickster; whys[3] now carries the 17s-to-13s figure.

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flags four names — 'His Crushing Blow', 'Hold Counter Strike', 'Use Warrior Trickster's' and 'His Warrior Trickster'. All four are the real ability names with a leading article or possessive; every one is a false positive.
audit.corrected: No name changes made on those four.
sources: packet.enemyAbilities: Crushing Blow, Warrior Trickster, Nimbus Strike, Cyclone, Stone Skin

edits.before: Trinity Force is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Nimbus Strike's cooldown.
edits.after: Warrior Trickster scales as juke and reset — the decoy eats your E, so hold it for the real Wukong.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Wukong carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in this is a coinflip decided by who lands their combo first — never spend Counter Strike or a leap on his decoy.

edits.before: His engage dash. E the follow-up. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His engage dash. Hold your 17s E for it, not for the decoy that follows.

edits.before: Ranking Counter Strike at 4-5 means it's up for more of his Nimbus Strike engages, so you keep punishing the dash and stay ahead.
edits.after: Ranking Counter Strike drops it from 17s to 13s by rank 3, so it covers more of his Nimbus Strike engages and you stay ahead of the dash.

edits.before: Both ult: bait his Cyclone (R) knock-up with E up, dodge the spin's autos, recast to stun him out of it, then pop Grandmaster at Arms for the armor/MR to win the all-in.
edits.after: Both ult: bait his Cyclone (R) knock-up with E up, dodge the spin's autos, recast to stun him out of it, then pop Grandmaster's Might for the armor/MR to win the all-in.

edits.before: This is a coinflip that leans your way on clean E timing. Levels 4-5 you rank the combo and Counter Strike is up more often, so keep baiting his Nimbus Strike and punishing the dash. At 6 you both ult: his Cyclone (R) is a spin knock-up all-in, but if you hold E for the moment he Cyclones in, you dodge the spin's autos, recast to stun him out of it, and pop Grandmaster at Arms for the armor/MR that turns the duel. The one mistake that loses this lane is blowing E or Q on the clone before his real engage.
edits.after: This is a coinflip that leans your way on clean E timing. Levels 4-5 you rank Counter Strike from 17s down to 13s, so it covers more of his Nimbus Strike engages and you keep punishing the dash. At 6 you both ult: his Cyclone (R) is a spin knock-up all-in, but if you hold E for the moment he Cyclones in, you dodge the spin's autos, recast to stun him out of it, and pop Grandmaster's Might for the armor/MR that turns the duel. The one mistake that loses this lane is blowing E or Q on the clone before his real engage.

edits.before: Past two items this stays a true coinflip decided by who lands their combo, since Wukong is item-dependent and not a hard scaler. Build your standard bruiser path — Trinity Force or Blade of the Ruined King into his health gives you a strong dueling spike, and Grandmaster at Arms' on-hit ramps your extended trades. Respect that his W decoy and stealth only get stronger as a juke and fight-reset with items; force your all-ins while his Cyclone is down, and never tunnel onto a clone in a teamfight.
edits.after: Past two items this stays a true coinflip decided by who lands their combo, since Wukong is item-dependent and not a hard scaler. Build your standard bruiser path — Trinity Force or Blade of the Ruined King into his health gives you a strong dueling spike, and Grandmaster's Might's every-third-hit on-hit ramps your extended trades. Respect that his W decoy and stealth only get stronger as a juke and fight-reset with items; force your all-ins while his Cyclone is down, and never tunnel onto a clone in a teamfight.

notes: enemyKit is null in this brief — no Wukong kit file was attached, so I had no cooldowns, ranges or flags for Crushing Blow, Warrior Trickster, Nimbus Strike, Cyclone or Stone Skin. Every number I added is a Jax number from the owner kit. That means several existing claims stayed unverified rather than being confirmed or fixed: that Crushing Blow shreds armor, that Warrior Trickster grants invisibility as well as a decoy, and that Cyclone knocks up. All are consistent with the packet's ability names and with each other, so I left them alone. If the kit can be attached, this matchup is worth a second pass purely to put his cooldowns on the page. All four packet suspectNames are false positives.
